recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-12252 unless OO later resolves a separate DeviceRequest naming or workflow issue that intentionally changes the current resource scope.
issue_request: FHIR-12252 was a Published/Persuasive OO change request for FHIR-core DeviceUseRequest. It requested changing the resource name to DeviceRequest and clarifying that the resource deals with allocation of a device to a patient, may include instructions for use, and leaves the logistics of getting the device to the patient to other resources.
initial_application: No source-history commit was found that explicitly names FHIR-12252. The apparent application is the January 9, 2017 DeviceUseRequest-to-DeviceRequest source work in commits 7bf0f7e00f13fcfaec67c9e17d8c89e75f3cf08a and 2d7f54c1d65906343cdc69a239a51781713be51f, whose subjects cite [#12552]. The first commit renamed the active resource folder and fhir.ini entries and changed the DeviceRequest boundaries prose to the requested allocation/instructions/logistics wording; the second updated a related diagram/translation surface.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists devicerequest=DeviceRequest in the active [resources] section, and source/devicerequest/structuredefinition-DeviceRequest.xml defines id, name, URL, and type as DeviceRequest. Remaining DeviceUseRequest strings are legacy compatibility records in the deleted-resource list, resource-name tracker, and old resource type code system. Later Zulip and OO Confluence evidence treats DeviceRequest as replacing DeviceUseRequest. FHIR-57360 was found as an unresolved Triaged issue, but it concerns the later DeviceRequest.code-to-product element rename rather than this resource rename and is not final.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The latest combined-branch source already reflects both halves of FHIR-12252: the active resource is DeviceRequest, and the current DeviceRequest introduction states that it deals with allocation of a device to a patient, may contain instructions for use, and addresses delivery/implantation/fulfillment logistics in other resources.

related_jiras.note: Unresolved Triaged R6 issue about the later DeviceRequest.code-to-product element rename; it does not alter this resource-rename audit.
